rejected.title: Development of a Continuous Glycolysis Process for the Recycling of Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) from Post-Consumer Polycotton Blended Textile Waste
rejected.reason: User-confirmed DOI exclusion: this continuous PET glycolysis/recycling process is outside the Organic Synthesis Gallery scope.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The 2026-10-05 prepublish review records the RSC article as a continuous twin-screw glycolysis process for PET in post-consumer polycotton textile waste. The chemical depolymerization is real, but the article's principal contribution is recycling/process engineering of a polymer waste stream rather than a general organic preparative method. The user explicitly states that this DOI does not count for the Gallery.
rejected.challengeReason: The strongest argument for inclusion is that PET ester bonds are chemically cleaved and the process is scalable. That does not override the user's DOI-level boundary, and this exclusion must not be generalized to all polymerization, depolymerization, or recycling chemistry.
rejected.evidenceLevel: fresh prepublish publisher abstract/article-specific primary-source evidence plus explicit user DOI decision

scopeAssessment.primaryContribution: Continuous glycolysis/recycling process development for PET in post-consumer polycotton textile waste.
scopeAssessment.preparativeTransformation: PET ester-bond cleavage by glycolysis in a continuous processing setup.
scopeAssessment.generalityEvidence: The prior review cited real waste-stream handling and continuous twin-screw processing, but not a general small-molecule preparative substrate-to-product scope.
scopeAssessment.sourceEvidence: 2026-10-05 prepublish review cites the RSC DOI/article page and records the publisher abstract facts about continuous glycolysis, PET/polycotton feed, and twin-screw extrusion.
scopeAssessment.boundaryChallenge: Chemical depolymerization and scale-up are genuine synthetic chemistry operations, but the explicit DOI-level user decision excludes this process-engineering/recycling article without creating a category-wide ban.

note: Only previously confirmed out-of-scope entries are removed. This does not claim a complete new discovery audit or global semantic closure.
